commandObservation.scope: The command snapshot was taken after both native captures and layer demotion. It is not a record of the earlier separate device-layer buffers.

conclusions: All136nativePNG and72compressed command-log hashes and uncompressed identities match. Independent pixel comparisons reproduce every stored result. All compared native Writing/device rectangles match exactly across implementations at every recorded stage.

One default initial section pair reproduces the exact earlier25303-pixel difference mask. It occurs on protected pair2 before the computed-font, FAQ, same-scroll or header preparations. The immediately following device clip has the exactLCD device band shared by all other default device captures.

The protected failing page retains four separate device drawing layers before capture. During the second clipped capture the document layer translates by the device clip371px offset and those four layers disappear. Native DOM geometry, styles, scroll, viewport, font state and animations are unchanged across all three readings except the performance timestamp.
Every device pair and every later section pair matches under the unchanged threshold. Header/FAQ preparations do not reproduce the transition in this fixed sequence.
The default grayscale question crop equals the disabledLCD question crop, but their whole-device bands differ. Text LCD permission alone does not explain every changed device pixel.
This supports a bounded native screenshot preparation investigation and contradicts a fixed source typography or composition discrepancy. It does not close the dedicated full Writing checkpoint.
causalLimits: The exact compositor lifecycle that retained the four device layers before capture is not established.

The second clipped screenshot, its temporary compositor translation, layer demotion and pixel transition occur in the same observed sequence; this record does not generalise that one observed transition into a guarantee for every width or browser.
Command snapshots are collected after both native captures. They verify the document commands after flattening, not the original cached buffers used by the soft section capture.
Stage operations are cumulative and instrumentation can affect paint scheduling. Initial screenshots already use clipped caret-hide preparation.

A prospective fixed preparation must retain its original evidence and strict full-section comparison. No frame should be chosen by agreement and no threshold, source style or runtime should be altered to conceal differences.
